messages:
sam: quick heads-up — spotted a blindspot when gateway replays/rewires streaming calls to a different upstream mid-flight. logs show trace continuity but billing/metrics split. we should sync on semantics. :thinking:
jia: can you paste the minimal repro? is this an ingress->egress failover or client reconnect scenario?
sam: ingress->egress failover. client keeps sending, gateway detects upstream drop and re-establishes with another pool. we reattach the client's stream but trailers from the original upstream are gone and the new upstream emits a different request-id. observability shows 2 upstreams for one client call.
marc: ouch. sounds like three concerns: observability/tracing continuity, idempotency/retry-safety, and billing attribution (tokens counted twice?).
anya: agree. also backpressure semantics: when we splice to new upstream do we replay buffered frames or resume from last acked offset? how do we represent that in telemetry so SRE can reason?
sam: minimal idea: carry a sideband set of headers that are gateway-controlled and survive upstream changes: ``x-rw-trace-id``, ``x-edge-resume-id``, ``x-edge-retry-count``. persist the mapping in the gateway state so metrics aggregate under `x-rw-trace-id` even if upstream IDs differ.
jia: leaving headers around is straightforward but curious about where to put final-delivery signals — trailers are natural but trailers are lost on midstream failover. can we emit a synthetic trailer from gateway if upstream trailer is missing?
marc: synthetic trailer makes sense for observability + billing. but it changes semantics: upstreams expect to own finality. need an invariant: gateway synthetic finalization must be honest (indicate it faked statuses). maybe use ``Grpc-Trailer-Proxy: synthetic`` and include original upstream status if we have it.
anya: and for idempotency: we must not auto-retry for endpoints with side-effects (webhooks, dataset writes). can we limit automatic reattach to pure-generation endpoints (text/embeddings) and make it configurable per route?
sam: yes — route-level flag `allow-stream-reattach`. default off for customer-defined routes; Redwood curated generation routes default on. will add guardrails.
ops-qa: question re billing: if client sends N tokens, upstream1 consumes M and upstream2 consumes K (M+K ~= N) — do we bill based on client tokens or upstream consumed tokens?
marc: we should bill based on upstream consumed tokens (actual compute), but provide a per-trace reconciliation view that shows client->gateway->upstream mapping with a synthetic final trailer that includes `client_tokens`, `upstream_tokens_total`, `replay_count`. example synthetic trailer:
```
Grpc-Trailer-Proxy: synthetic
x-client-tokens: 1532
x-upstream-tokens-total: 1536
x-edge-replay-count: 1
```
This lets billing backend attribute compute correctly while UX shows small discrepancies due to replay.
jia: tests to catch regressions: simulate midstream TCP drop, enforce new upstream emits different req-id, ensure metrics merge under `x-rw-trace-id` and gateway emits a synthetic trailer when upstream final trailer missing.
sam: action items: I'll sketch a tiny PoC that sets ``x-rw-trace-id`` and emits synthetic trailers on splice. Marc — can you draft an RFC for header names + semantic invariants? Jia — add integration tests in gateway harness. Anya — enumerate routes that must opt-out.
marc: will do RFC. include how this affects trace sampling and retention. also add a small note: preserve client-visible error classes (e.g., `retryable` vs `hard-fail`) so product teams can rely on stable signals.
deploy-bot: Deploy notice: canary edge v2.14 rolling out to 5% — watch for increases in `Grpc-Trailer-Proxy: synthetic`.
ops-qa: will add dashboards for synthetic-trailer-rate + per-route reattach counts. when do we want to ship this canary?
sam: aiming to land PoC + tests this sprint, RFC early next week, canary after safety review. :thumbsup:
